newsitem.title: netherlands: IATA unit to study airfreight market rates system.
newsitem.headline: IATA unit to study airfreight market rates system.

text.p: International Airline Publications B.V. (IAP), which publishes the official IATA air freight tariffs, is studying the possibility of developing a computer-based market rates information system.

Product manager Hans Tiessen told Reuters in a telephone interview IAP had launched a study to weigh up a system in which airlines would contribute real time price information about air freight rates and destinations.
"I know that some airlines have indicated that they would be interested in such a system," Tiessen said, adding that the study could take two to three years to complete.
Tiessen said each contributing airline would determine who could access its sensitive market information.

"We do not envisage a service where airlines would examine each other's rates. Airline A might store its information on the system for access by Shipper B. Only those with permission would be able to access that information," he said.
Tiessen said such a system would boost transparency between airlines and shipper customers. The airline could also allow access to forwarders or agents with which it did regular business.
Competing airlines would be denied access to their rivals' rate information, he said.

IAP will shortly move from its offices in Hoofdorp to new premises at Schiphol airport. The group, which employs 33 staff, is to re-locate to the Triport building at the Dutch national airport on January 24, Tiessen said.
